# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…

/// ponytail: openai-completions dialect only (the default custom-provider

/// brand-typed catalog names forward while anthropic/google/chatgpt-
/// responses reject); other wire dialects answer with a clean llmRes
/// error until a second dialect is actually needed.
Future<void> relayOpenAiCompletion(
  LlmRelayRequest request,
  void Function(String delta) onDelta, {
  http.Client? client,
  Duration? idleTimeout,
}) async {
  // The key is injected server-side; a null key is the ANONYMOUS relay
  // mode — the call goes out with no Authorization header and can never
  // carry a stored key (SEC-01).
  final response = await sendProviderRequest(
    client ?? sharedProviderHttpClient(),
    _relayCall(request, request.key),
    null,
  );
  await _forwardDeltas(
    createSseIterator(response, null, idleTimeout: idleTimeout),
    onDelta,
  );
}

The only synchronous throw is `"Already waiting for next."` (concurrent moveNext). That's intended (the timeout supersedes) — and importantly the late error is not unhandled since it's consumed by `.then(onError:)` ✓. But the underlying live error gets silently eaten when the watchdog wins the race — the user sees TimeoutException instead of the real ClientException. Minor UX nuance, intended design ("event-level silence is the honest signal").

## PR Description

Fixes #921.

## Reproduced
The `crash.log` attached to the issue shows the same unhandled error twice (`ClientException: Connection closed while receiving data, uri=https://api.z.ai/...`, v0.1.385 on 09-15 and v1.0.471 on 09-24) with a stack that ends in the root zone — no harness frames. Regression test reproduces it deterministically: idle-watchdog timeout abandons the SSE iteration, then the dying link's error escapes the zone (fails pre-fix, passes post-fix).

## Root cause
`fa crashed` was not the network error itself — it was an **unhandled zone error** from an orphaned byte pipeline:

1. A silent endpoint trips the stream-idle watchdog (the issue's `TimeoutException ... 300s`), which surfaces gracefully — but abandons the SSE iteration **without cancelling the cancel token**.
2. The `async*` `SseDecoder` cannot finish cancelling while it is suspended awaiting input, so the byte pipeline (`response.stream → utf8 → SseDecoder`) stays attached to the socket with its terminal listener gone.
3. `runProviderStream.finally` closes the owned HTTP client (or the flaky link dies on its own — 'low internet'); the teardown error flows through the still-live forwarding subs into a handlerless chain → root zone → `fa crashed`.
4. The old byte-level swallow guarded only `cancelToken.isCancelled` (the abort path), and the `unawaited` cancel futures were additional unhandled-error vectors.

## Fix (`createSseIterator`, one source, all adapters)
- The raw body subscription is **owned** with a stable `onError`: late errors are swallowed once the stream is abandoned (idle-watchdog fire, iterator cancel, token hook) or the token is cancelled; live errors still ride into the pipeline for the adapters' errors-as-events try/catch.
- `onDone` is always forwarded — it is what unsticks the pending lazy cancellation, so nothing leaks.
- Cancel futures are quiet-cancelled (failure is noise, never an unawaited-error crash).
- All `createSseIterator` consumers inherit the fix (openai-completions/z.ai, anthropic, google, dial, browser llm-relay).

## Not implicated
#914 (ce2e27c, filed-2-minutes-before suspicion) is test-only (`test/integration/` + ci workflow) and cannot produce this runtime path; the crash log predates it (same signature on 09-15, v0.1.385).

## Delivered
- Failing-first regression tests in `test/providers/sse_idle_watchdog_test.dart` (idle-watchdog, cancel-mid-stream, token-abort); scoped provider suites green: 209 passed / 0 failed.
- `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` applied on touched files.

## Remaining
- The recurring `Bad state: connection closed` crashes in the same log (v0.1.369–0.406, Sept 14–17) have empty stacks and predate those versions; not reproduced here — worth its own issue if still seen on ≥1.0.471.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…

/// ponytail: openai-completions dialect only (the default custom-provider
/// norm — openai/openrouter/zai/minimax/aiin/kimi endpoints; the catalog
/// gate in [resolveLlmRelayTarget] enforces it by wire dialect, so
/// brand-typed catalog names forward while anthropic/google/chatgpt-
/// responses reject); other wire dialects answer with a clean llmRes
/// error until a second dialect is actually needed.
Future<void> relayOpenAiCompletion(
  LlmRelayRequest request,
  void Function(String delta) onDelta, {
  http.Client? client,
  Duration? idleTimeout,
}) async {
  // The key is injected server-side; a null key is the ANONYMOUS relay
  // mode — the call goes out with no Authorization header and can never
  // carry a stored key (SEC-01).
  final response = await sendProviderRequest(
    client ?? sharedProviderHttpClient(),
    _relayCall(request, request.key),
    null,
  );
  await _forwardDeltas(
    createSseIterator(response, null, idleTimeout: idleTimeout),
    onDelta,
  );
}

This matters for the body controller: when the adapter has consumed an event and is processing it (between moveNext calls), the transformed stream is paused → pause propagates to `body`'s subscription → `onPause: () => rawSub?.pause()` → the raw socket stream is paused. Backpressure preserved.

messages.preview: SDK semantics confirmed: `moveNext()` after `cancel()` returns a completed `false` future (no throw). Let me run the final verification pass — format check, plus the browser-relay consumer's SSE path:

blocks.text:
`_initializeOrDone`: after cancel, `_stateData == null` → falls through to the done case → returns a completed-false future. So `moveNext()` after `cancel()` returns `false` (completed future) — **no synchronous throw**. 

The only synchronous throw is `"Already waiting for next."` (concurrent moveNext). In the wrapper: if an adapter called `moveNext()` while a previous moveNext future is still pending — the wrapper arms the timer, then `_inner.moveNext()` throws synchronously → propagates out of the wrapper's `moveNext()` → caught by the adapter/runProviderStream ✓ BUT the timer stays armed with an unlistened completer → later `completer.completeError(TimeoutException)` → unhandled async error.

Is concurrent moveNext possible in-repo? The adapters all `await` moveNext in a while loop — no concurrency. So it's a latent robustness gap, pre-existing in structure (the timer+completer pattern predates the PR — only the timer callback body changed). SUGGESTION.

Now, let me also double-check the case where `completer.completeError` fires when the caller DID get the future but already stopped listening? The caller always gets `completer.future` (return statement reached) unless the sync throw above. If the adapter awaits it → handled ✓.

One more check — `moveNext()` wrapper when `_inner.moveNext()` completes with error AFTER the timer already fired (timeout won the race): the `.then` onError handler: `_timer?.cancel()` (already fired — cancel no-op), `if (!completer.isCompleted)` — already completed with TimeoutException → error DROPPED silently. That's intended (the timeout supersedes) — and importantly the late error is not unhandled since it's consumed by `.then(onError:)` ✓. But the underlying live error gets silently eaten when the watchdog wins the race — the user sees TimeoutException instead of the real ClientException. Minor UX nuance, intended design ("event-level silence is the honest signal").

Now — `_quietCancel` swallows `_inner.cancel()` failures wholesale. From the SDK `cancel()`: returns `subscription.cancel()` — for a transform pipeline over `body` controller — cancellation futures of controllers complete normally; rawSub.cancel() could complete with an error if the underlying (response.stream) cancel fails — swallowed by design (noise). ✓ documented.

Now I have the full picture. Let me consolidate the exhaustive single-pass findings:

## Findings assessment

**Verified working:**
- analyze clean, format clean, 6/6 new tests pass, 469/469 provider suite passes.
- Fix mechanism is sound: owned subscription with stable `onError` + abandonment flag + always-forwarded `onDone` + quiet cancel futures.
- Contract-safe: `StreamIterator.cancel()` idempotent (SDK-verified); `moveNext()` after cancel returns false-future.
- All 4 `createSseIterator` consumers (openai-completions incl. z.ai/dial, anthropic, google, browser llm-relay) inherit the fix.
- Backward compat: documented abort-path swallow (`cancelToken.isCancelled`) preserved; live errors still forwarded with stack traces.
- Tests: deterministic (synchronous flag set before async injects), guarded-zone verification, reasonable settle delays.
- CI: no `ci_failures.md` input → nothing blocking from CI. The discussions show red-validation runs triaged as ambient PTY/perf failures in files untouched by this diff (credible: `ctrl_c_double_press_test.dart` ACX.3 and `perf_open_gate_test.dart`, `job_board_stability_pty_test.dart` — none provider/SSE-related; provider suites green in the same runs).

**Candidate findings:**

1. **SUGGESTION — `onData` doesn't guard `body.isClosed`** (line 780): `onError` checks `body.isClosed` before `addError`, but `onData` only checks `!abandoned`. A stream that (contractually shouldn't, but misbehaving ones do — the SDK even comments about "really misbehaving streams") emits data after done would make `body.add` throw a synchronous `StateError` inside the raw subscription's data handler → an unhandled zone error — exactly the crash class this PR eliminates. One-word hardening: `if (!abandoned && !body.isClosed)`. Very low probability (http package streams are well-behaved), so SUGGESTION.

2. **SUGGESTION — orphaned idle timer if `_inner.moveNext()` throws synchronously** (lines 834-844): the wrapper arms `_timer` before calling `_inner.moveNext()`; the SDK's `StreamIterator.moveNext` throws synchronously on a concurrent call ("Already waiting for next"). If that ever happened, the sync exception escapes `moveNext()` before `return completer.future`, leaving the timer armed with a completer no one awaits → 5 minutes later `completer.completeError` fires on an unlistened future → an unhandled async error of exactly the class this PR fixes. Pre-existing structure (only the timer callback body changed), and no in-repo adapter ever makes concurrent moveNext calls, so SUGGESTION (wrap the inner call or complete the completer on the sync path).

3. **SUGGESTION — `_IdleWatchdogSseIterator.cancel()` returns the raw `_inner.cancel()` future** (line 869): per the PR's own comment, "the cancel future rides that dying pipeline and may itself fail". The token path quiets it (line 805) and the watchdog quiets it (839), but the public `cancel()` future still can complete with an error; any future caller doing `await iterator.cancel()` (or `unawaited(iterator.cancel())` — the old crash pattern) re-imports the bug. Consider returning the quieted future from `cancel()` itself. Currently no in-repo caller awaits it raw (tests await it — but in tests the pipeline is a controller, cancel succeeds), so SUGGESTION.

4. **SUGGESTION (test) — no test asserts the "onDone always forwarded / no leaked subscription" claim**: the PR description says onDone forwarding "is what unsticks the pending lazy cancellation, so nothing leaks", but there's no regression test asserting the abandoned pipeline fully cancels rawSub (e.g., `await rawSubDone` or controller.onCancel bookkeeping). If someone later "simplifies" onDone away, no test fails. Minor.

5. **GENERAL comment (unchanged code, outside diff)**: `chatgpt_codex.dart`'s `_consumeStream` uses its own `await for ... transform(utf8.decoder).transform(const LineSplitter())` loop — no idle watchdog (a silent Codex endpoint hangs the turn indefinitely — the very symptom class the watchdog exists for) and its own hand-rolled SSE parsing (`_SseAccumulator`) instead of `SseDecoder`/`createSseIterator`. Its cancel path is prompt (non-generator transformers cancel synchronously, no lazy-cancel orphan), so it's NOT part of this crash, but the divergence is worth a follow-up issue. This belongs in pr_review_general.md, not an inline comment (outside diff).

6. Observation on behavior: when the watchdog wins the race against a live error, the real error is superseded by TimeoutException (intended per design comments). Not a finding.

7. Security: no secrets/logging changes; error messages don't leak tokens; the test URL is inert. Nothing to flag.

8. Ticket AC check: The ticket IS issue #921 (the PR description doubles as the ticket). ACs: reproduce ✓ (failing-first test claim; the regression tests are in place and pass), fix at one source ✓, scoped suites green ✓ (verified 469), analyze/format ✓ (verified). The "Remaining" note about `Bad state: connection closed` is honestly deferred with a suggestion to file a separate issue — fine.

Severity classification: No BLOCKING (fix is correct, tests pass, CI red is credibly ambient and not input as ci_failures.md). No IMPORTANT honestly? Let me reconsider #2 and #3 — are they IMPORTANT ("real maintainability or correctness issue")?

#2: unreachable in current code (no concurrent moveNext). It's a latent hazard in error handling of exactly the crash class being fixed. I'd rate SUGGESTION given in-repo callers all await serially. Hmm — "when in doubt, start one level higher". Is there doubt? The wrapper's contract is a StreamIterator; StreamIterator.moveNext is documented "Calling moveNext again while a previous call has not completed is an error". No in-repo caller violates it. I'll keep SUGGESTION but note it prominently.

#3: currently only the token path and tests call cancel(); the token path quiets. Future callers might not. SUGGESTION.

#1: defensive hardening, SUGGESTION.

So: 0 blocking, 0 important... hmm, wait. Let me think harder about whether anything rises to IMPORTANT.

Reconsider the swallow condition `body.isClosed` in onError — is there a LIVE error swallowed incorrectly? `body.isClosed` becomes true only after onDone ran (normal EOS). After EOS, no errors can arrive. So no.

Reconsider `abandoned` semantics vs the adapters' "dataChunks == 0" empty-stream detection (openai_completions): watchdog timeout → TimeoutException thrown from moveNext → propagates out of `_consumeSse` → runProviderStream ErrorEvent. Unchanged from before (old code also cancelled inner). ✓

What about the case where abandonment happens via token cancel while the adapter is BLOCKED in moveNext with pending data? E.g., adapter awaiting moveNext; token fires → abandon → iterator.cancel() → `_inner.cancel()` → SDK cancel(): `_subscription != null`, `!_hasValue` → pending moveNext future `_asyncComplete(false)` → adapter's `while` loop exits normally → anthropic checks `cancelToken?.isCancelled` → AbortedError ✓. Unchanged behavior.

One more potential issue: **double `iterator.cancel()` invocation** — watchdog fired (quiet-cancel of `_inner.cancel()`) AND token path calls `iterator.cancel()` → `_IdleWatchdogSseIterator.cancel()` → `return _inner.cancel()` → SDK returns `Future._nullFuture` (idempotent) → the token chain's `.then((_) {}, onError:)` handles it anyway ✓.

**Memory**: `body` controller holds buffered events if the chain never subscribes (first moveNext never called) — pre-existing equivalent. Skip.

**Perf**: one extra controller hop per event — negligible vs network SSE. Skip.

**Duplication**: none introduced; `_quietCancel` is a shared helper (could be top-level in a util but it's private single-use file — fine).

**Naming**: `abandoned`/`abandon`/`onAbandon`/`_quietCancel` — consistent with the PR/domain language ✓.

**Docs**: doc comment updated thoroughly; issue references consistent (#921) ✓.

**Workflow/CI**: no workflow changes in this PR ✓.

So final counts: blocking 0, important 0, suggestions 4 (3 code + 1 test), plus 1 general-comment observation (codex adapter divergence).

Recommendation: APPROVE (no blocking issues). The general guideline…

- **Title**: fix(921): swallow post-abandonment SSE transport errors instead of crashing
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/921-cli-crash` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +164
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-09-24T17:33:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-24T19:39:03Z

## PR Description

Fixes #921.

## Reproduced
The `crash.log` attached to the issue shows the same unhandled error twice (`ClientException: Connection closed while receiving data, uri=https://api.z.ai/...`, v0.1.385 on 09-15 and v1.0.471 on 09-24) with a stack that ends in the root zone — no harness frames. Regression test reproduces it deterministically: idle-watchdog timeout abandons the SSE iteration, then the dying link's error escapes the zone (fails pre-fix, passes post-fix).

## Root cause
`fa crashed` was not the network error itself — it was an **unhandled zone error** from an orphaned byte pipeline:

1. A silent endpoint trips the stream-idle watchdog (the issue's `TimeoutException ... 300s`), which surfaces gracefully — but abandons the SSE iteration **without cancelling the cancel token**.
2. The `async*` `SseDecoder` cannot finish cancelling while it is suspended awaiting input, so the byte pipeline (`response.stream → utf8 → SseDecoder`) stays attached to the socket with its terminal listener gone.
3. `runProviderStream.finally` closes the owned HTTP client (or the flaky link dies on its own — 'low internet'); the teardown error flows through the still-live forwarding subs into a handlerless chain → root zone → `fa crashed`.
4. The old byte-level swallow guarded only `cancelToken.isCancelled` (the abort path), and the `unawaited` cancel futures were additional unhandled-error vectors.

## Fix (`createSseIterator`, one source, all adapters)
- The raw body subscription is **owned** with a stable `onError`: late errors are swallowed once the stream is abandoned (idle-watchdog fire, iterator cancel, token hook) or the token is cancelled; live errors still ride into the pipeline for the adapters' errors-as-events try/catch.
- `onDone` is always forwarded — it is what unsticks the pending lazy cancellation, so nothing leaks.
- Cancel futures are quiet-cancelled (failure is noise, never an unawaited-error crash).
- All `createSseIterator` consumers inherit the fix (openai-completions/z.ai, anthropic, google, dial, browser llm-relay).

## Not implicated
#914 (ce2e27c, filed-2-minutes-before suspicion) is test-only (`test/integration/` + ci workflow) and cannot produce this runtime path; the crash log predates it (same signature on 09-15, v0.1.385).

## Delivered
- Failing-first regression tests in `test/providers/sse_idle_watchdog_test.dart` (idle-watchdog, cancel-mid-stream, token-abort); scoped provider suites green: 209 passed / 0 failed.
- `dart analyze` clean, `dart format` applied on touched files.

## Remaining
- The recurring `Bad state: connection closed` crashes in the same log (v0.1.369–0.406, Sept 14–17) have empty stacks and predate those versions; not reproduced here — worth its own issue if still seen on ≥1.0.471.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200

  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.

Future<void> relayOpenAiCompletion(
  LlmRelayRequest request,
  void Function(String delta) onDelta, {
  http.Client? client,
  Duration? idleTimeout,
}) async {
  // The key is injected server-side; a null key is the ANONYMOUS relay

  final response = await sendProviderRequest(
    client ?? sharedProviderHttpClient(),
    _relayCall(request, request.key),
    null,
  );
  await _forwardDeltas(
    createSseIterator(response, null, idleTimeout: idleTimeout),
    onDelta,
  );
}

blocks.text:
The test hung — interesting. `await c.close()` — the controller can't close while a listener exists? Actually `c.close()` waits for... `close()` returns a future that completes when the listener has received the done event. `gen(c)`'s await-for subscribed to c.stream; `it2.cancel()` → lazy cancel of the generator; the await-for inside the generator cancels its subscription to c.stream... then `c.close()` completes. Then `await cf` — the cancel future... then `await mv == false` — mv completed false? Hmm, but `await mv == false` is parsed as `await (mv == false)` → mv is a Future, `Future == false` is false, then `await false` — prints `false`. My bad on precedence. But the hang means something didn't complete — possibly `await cf` (the cancel future) never completed because the generator is suspended awaiting input and closing the controller... hmm, actually the hang is a great empirical probe of the lazy-cancel semantics!

Wait — actually the order: `await c.close()` — close() returns done future completing when the done event is delivered to the listener (the generator's await-for). If the generator's await-for subscription was already cancelled (by the cancel command), does close() still complete? For a single-subscription controller with a cancelled subscription, close() future completes... it should.

Then `await cf` — cancel future of the generator stream. The generator is suspended awaiting the next event from src. Cancel command resumes the generator → await-for exits → cancels src subscription → generator body completes → cancel future completes. BUT — if the done event from close() was delivered FIRST (resuming the await-for loop normally to exit), then the generator completes normally, and `it2.cancel()` after the stream is done returns a completed future. Now I have the full picture. Let me consolidate the exhaustive single-pass findings:

## Findings assessment

**Verified working:**
- analyze clean, format clean, 6/6 new tests pass, 469/469 provider suite passes.
- Fix mechanism is sound: owned subscription with stable `onError` + abandonment flag + always-forwarded `onDone` + quiet cancel futures.
- Contract-safe: `StreamIterator.cancel()` idempotent (SDK-verified); `moveNext()` after cancel returns false-future.
- All 4 `createSseIterator` consumers (openai-completions incl. z.ai/dial, anthropic, google, browser llm-relay) inherit the fix.
- Backward compat: documented abort-path swallow (`cancelToken.isCancelled`) preserved; live errors still forwarded with stack traces.
- Tests: deterministic (synchronous flag set before async injects), guarded-zone verification, reasonable settle delays.
- CI: no `ci_failures.md` input → nothing blocking from CI. The discussions show red-validation runs triaged as ambient PTY/perf failures in files untouched by this diff (credible: `ctrl_c_double_press_test.dart` ACX.3 and `perf_open_gate_test.dart`, `job_board_stability_pty_test.dart` — none provider/SSE-related; provider suites green in the same runs).

**Candidate findings:**

1. **SUGGESTION — `onData` doesn't guard `body.isClosed`** (line 780): `onError` checks `body.isClosed` before `addError`, but `onData` only checks `!abandoned`. A stream that (contractually shouldn't, but misbehaving ones do — the SDK even comments about "really misbehaving streams") emits data after done would make `body.add` throw a synchronous `StateError` inside the raw subscription's data handler → an unhandled zone error — exactly the crash class this PR eliminates. One-word hardening: `if (!abandoned && !body.isClosed)`. Very low probability (http package streams are well-behaved), so SUGGESTION.

2. **SUGGESTION — orphaned idle timer if `_inner.moveNext()` throws synchronously** (lines 834-844): the wrapper arms `_timer` before calling `_inner.moveNext()`; the SDK's `StreamIterator.moveNext` throws synchronously on a concurrent call ("Already waiting for next"). If that ever happened, the sync exception escapes `moveNext()` before `return completer.future`, leaving the timer armed with a completer no one awaits → 5 minutes later `completer.completeError` fires on an unlistened future → an unhandled async error of exactly the class this PR fixes. Pre-existing structure (only the timer callback body changed), and no in-repo adapter ever makes concurrent moveNext calls, so SUGGESTION (wrap the inner call or complete the completer on the sync path).

3. **SUGGESTION — `_IdleWatchdogSseIterator.cancel()` returns the raw `_inner.cancel()` future** (line 869): per the PR's own comment, "the cancel future rides that dying pipeline and may itself fail". The token path quiets it (line 805) and the watchdog quiets it (839), but the public `cancel()` future still can complete with an error; any future caller doing `await iterator.cancel()` (or `unawaited(iterator.cancel())` — the old crash pattern) re-imports the bug. Consider returning the quieted future from `cancel()` itself. Currently no in-repo caller awaits it raw (tests await it — but in tests the pipeline is a controller, cancel succeeds), so SUGGESTION.

4. **SUGGESTION (test) — no test asserts the "onDone always forwarded / no leaked subscription" claim**: the PR description says onDone forwarding "is what unsticks the pending lazy cancellation, so nothing leaks", but there's no regression test asserting the abandoned pipeline fully cancels rawSub (e.g., `await rawSubDone` or controller.onCancel bookkeeping). If someone later "simplifies" onDone away, no test fails. Minor.

5. **GENERAL comment (unchanged code, outside diff)**: `chatgpt_codex.dart`'s `_consumeStream` uses its own `await for ... transform(utf8.decoder).transform(const LineSplitter())` loop — no idle watchdog (a silent Codex endpoint hangs the turn indefinitely — the very symptom class the watchdog exists for) and its own hand-rolled SSE parsing (`_SseAccumulator`) instead of `SseDecoder`/`createSseIterator`. Its cancel path is prompt (non-generator transformers cancel synchronously, no lazy-cancel orphan), so it's NOT part of this crash, but the divergence is worth a follow-up issue. This belongs in pr_review_general.md, not an inline comment (outside diff).

6. Observation on behavior: when the watchdog wins the race against a live error, the real error is superseded by TimeoutException (intended per design comments). Not a finding.

7. Security: no secrets/logging changes; error messages don't leak tokens; the test URL is inert. Nothing to flag.
